name: JSON-LD
description: Serializes entities to JSON-LD / LDP for the Islandora Project.
provides_services: jsonld.contextgenerator (JsonldContextGenerator — builds a JSON-LD @context for an entity_type.bundle)
ecosystem_note: A serialization back end, not an end-user feature. It registers a `jsonld` serializer format (normalizers priority 10-20 + an encoder) that turns any ContentEntity into a JSON-LD `@graph` document, driven ENTIRELY by the core RDF module's field-to-RDF-property mappings: only fields that have an RDF mapping on their bundle are emitted, and the bundle's rdf:type(s) become the `@type`. Built for Islandora / Fedora (LDP) so a Drupal node round-trips as Linked Data. Ships no routes that output entity JSON-LD itself — you obtain JSON-LD by requesting an entity with `?_format=jsonld` (needs a REST/JSON-LD-aware route) or by calling the `serializer` service with format `jsonld`. It also exposes a context endpoint at `/jsonld/context/{entity_type}/{bundle}`. Depends on hal (link manager for entity/type URIs) and rdf (mappings + namespaces). By default every generated `@id` gets a `?_format=jsonld` suffix; a settings checkbox strips it. Field-level view access IS enforced during normalization.
project_description:
JSON-LD (JavaScript Object Notation for Linking Data) is a lightweight Linked Data format that gives your data context. It is easy for humans to read and write. It is easy for machines to parse and generate.

 This module provides a JSON-LD format for REST via a custom serializer that uses your site's RDF mappings. It also provides an alter to let your own module customize the JSON-LD beyond what RDF mappings can support. 

 To view the JSON-LD output, use the ?_format=jsonld query parameter after your entity URI, for example node/1?_format=jsonld .

 Although this module has been developed as part of the Islandora ecosystem, it has no dependencies on Islandora and can be used on its own.

 Development is done on Github.com so please contribute PRs there rather than MRs here.
